title: Unreadable regrade roots are reported as verified
claim: The production regrade command converts a missing or unreadable trials directory into an empty successful report and exit code 0 instead of failing closed at the evidence boundary.

evidence.detail: OfflineRegrader derives verified whenever failures is empty, while read_trial_ids maps every read_dir error to an empty vector with unwrap_or_default().
The CLI declares an I/O error but the production regrade path cannot produce it; a missing root therefore serializes outcome=verified and exits 0.
The adjacent report command rejects the same missing trials root, demonstrating an available fail-closed counterexample rather than an intentional empty-root convention.

reproduction: cargo run -q -p opi-eval -- report --root <the-same-nonexistent-absolute-directory> -> cannot read run root: run root ... holds no trials directory, nonzero exit

title: Rejected trial-identity reuse mutates the existing trial
claim: A second run using an already reserved trial identity creates directories and overwrites that trial's bench.toml before checking bundle/intent.json and rejecting reuse, so a rejected request silently changes existing Eval configuration/evidence.

evidence.detail: run_trial creates the trial workspace/trace/isolation directories and writes bench.toml at lines 1104-1127; only afterward does it test the durable intent and return the identity-reuse error.
The reuse test asserts exit 2 and preservation of bundle/manifest.json only; it does not compare the whole trial tree or bench.toml, so the mutation is not detected.

reproduction: Run opi-eval run with the absolute local-paired.toml config, absolute fixtures root, and a fresh run root; after the completed run, replace trials/trial-opi-1/bench.toml with sentinel-opi.

Run the identical command against the same root: it exits 2 with 'already has a durable intent reservation', but trials/trial-opi-1/bench.toml now contains '# assembled-run fixture config (never a user config)' instead of sentinel-opi.
